name: rebootclean
description:
A DELIBERATE REBOOT LEAVES THE ROOT CLEAN, which is the invariant BSD has and the reason a reboot is not a crash.  2.11BSD update #456 puts fsclean() in boot(); FGX's _Sys_Reboot reaches it through far slot 37.

The assertion is on the SECOND boot: `file system is clean; not checking' can only appear there, because boot one's rc remounts the root read-write and that clears the on-disk flag.  So seeing it after a reboot means the shutdown put it back.  Without fsclean the same run shows the full five-phase check instead -- correct, and over 45 seconds of it.

`UNEXPECTED INCONSISTENCY' is the other half: a reboot that leaves damage behind would be a reboot marked clean over a filesystem nobody checked, which is worse than the slow boot it replaced.

screen_contains: file system is clean; not checking
